idiom_name: pthread fan-out: pthread_create children + pthread_join before every return + shared stop flag
implementation_notes: POSIX threads provide primitives only, so the scope is a function-level discipline: record every child's pthread_t, and pthread_join each one before returning on every path (single cleanup label, or a join helper invoked from each exit). There is no scope object and no automatic failure propagation, so add a shared stop flag that children poll at safe points and, after a child failure, set the flag and keep joining. pthread_cancel is not a structured mechanism - asynchronous cancellation can terminate a child in an inconsistent state - so treat it as a last resort behind cleanup handlers.
pitfalls: A child that is never joined becomes a zombie thread and its stack and exit status leak (pthread_join(3)); joining is the only way to release those resources.
Children that never check the stop flag make the join loop block forever - cancellation is cooperative and there is no safe forced stop.
Returning from an error path before joining leaves children running with pointers into the caller's stack frame.
pthread_cancel at an arbitrary point can leave mutexes locked or state half-written; cancellation points have to be controlled explicitly.
